name: בָּרוּךְ
summary: Chiefly Baruch son of Neriah, Jeremiah's scribe: he received the deeds of Jeremiah's purchase, to keep them in an earthen vessel (Jer 32:12–14), wrote Jeremiah's words from his mouth on a scroll and read them in the house of Yahweh, and wrote them again after the king burned the scroll (Jer 36:4, 10, 32); Yahweh hid him and Jeremiah from the king (Jer 36:26), he was carried with Jeremiah to Egypt (Jer 43:6–7), and Yahweh promised him his life as a spoil wherever he went (Jer 45:1–5). Also Baruch son of Zabbai, who repaired the wall (Neh 3:20), a priest who sealed the covenant (Neh 10:7, 9), and Baruch son of Col-hozeh of Judah (Neh 11:5). The name is בָּרוּךְ, the passive participle of the verb, “blessed”, as in “blessed is the man who trusts in Yahweh” (Jer 17:7); scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: “I gave the deed of purchase אֶל־בָּרוּךְ בֶּן־נֵרִיָּה בֶּן־מַחְסֵיָה.”
“Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah, and Baruch wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of Yahweh … on a scroll.”
Baruch read the words of Jeremiah from the book in the house of Yahweh, in the ears of all the people.
The king ordered Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet seized, “but Yahweh hid them”.
Jeremiah gave another scroll to Baruch, who wrote on it all the words of the burned book, and many more.
The captains: “Baruch son of Neriah sets you against us.”
Baruch son of Neriah taken with Jeremiah into Egypt.
The word to Baruch: “Do you seek great things for yourself? Do not seek them … but I will give you your life as a spoil in all places where you go.”
“Baruch son of Zabbai earnestly repaired another section.”
Among those who sealed the covenant: “Daniel, Ginnethon, Baruch”; “these were the priests” (Neh 10:9).
“Maaseiah son of Baruch son of Col-hozeh.”
The word the name is: “בָּרוּךְ הַגֶּבֶר who trusts in Yahweh.”

note: b.dd.ae counts 82 tokens: 26 are the name (Jer 32:12–45:2; Neh 3:20; 10:7; 11:5), the other 56 are the participle בָּרוּךְ, which the verb's b.dd.aa also counts. TIPNR's Baruch@Neh.10.6 is Neh 10:7 in the Hebrew numbering. MACULA's Septuagint alignment gives βαρουξ. Phoenician has a short name BRK of the type brk-DN (Krahmalkov p. 126), but it is read there as active (“Birrek”), not passive.
